messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — Dedicated pool 'resv-east-2' GPU utilization >95% for 6m; request queue depth increasing. Top affected tenant: AcmeBank (reserved contract). Autoscaler attempted scale but failed: quota error. See runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-capacity

alice-oncall: @incident-bot got it. I'm on pager. Initial question: is this noisy-tenant eviction or autoscaler outage?

bob-runtime: logs show repeated allocation failures from provisioner: 
```
provisioner: allocate_failed pool=resv-east-2 reason=quota_exceeded code=429
autoscaler: scale_attempt id=kt-8234 status=failed
```

claire-infra: Confirming — cloud account hit GPU quota for the region. Autoscaler retried 3x and then gave up. No RBAC errors.

dave-support: AcmeBank is reporting increased 5xxs and long tail latencies. Support ticket #7892 opened — customer impact: degraded throughput for reserved endpoints.

erin-cs: I'm drafting a customer update. Key facts: reserved pool saturated, we're applying mitigations; no data loss; best-effort traffic may be throttled. Will ping account exec.

alice-oncall: Immediate mitigations: 1) apply tenant-level emergency throttling for best-effort routes 2) attempt manual cold-start of standby pool resv-east-3 3) fallback routing to hosted tier for non-sensitive calls. Assigning tasks.

bob-runtime: Trying manual scale command to add capacity:
```
infractl scale-pool --pool resv-east-2 --gpus 8 --force --reason "emergency surge"
```
Command returns: `error: quota exceeded for project`

claire-infra: Working with cloud console to request quota bump; ETA ~20-30m if approved. Meanwhile we can cold-start resv-east-3 but it has no reservations for AcmeBank; need to update routing to let them use resv-east-3 as temporary.

frank-platform: I can flip routing for AcmeBank to resv-east-3 as an emergency override. That will preserve reserved isolation but violates strict placement guarantees. Confirming risk with @erin-cs.

erin-cs: AcmeBank: prefer isolation but will accept temporary move if it restores SLA. Authorize route change. I'll notify them immediately.

alice-oncall: @frank-platform proceed. Add canary 10% first, monitor for errors and perf. If green, shift 100%. Use circuit breaker at 90th percentile latency.

bob-runtime: Implemented canary routing change: 
```
runtimectl route update --tenant acmebank --from resv-east-2 --to resv-east-3 --percent 10
```
Monitoring: 10% traffic to resv-east-3, CPU/GPU usage rising but within limits. Error rate for those requests = 0.8% (baseline 0.2%).

dave-support: Customer on phone wants ETA. Erin sent initial note. They asked if throttling will impact batch jobs; looks like yes for some backfills.

erin-cs: Sending update to AcmeBank: "We are diverting a small fraction of your traffic to a standby reserved pool; this should reduce errors. We anticipate full failover in ~15-30m. No data loss. We'll keep you updated every 15m."

alice-oncall: Canary looks good after +12m: latency stable, errors down. Proceeding to shift 100% and enable emergency quota protections.

bob-runtime: Switched to 100%. Command: 
```
runtimectl route update --tenant acmebank --from resv-east-2 --to resv-east-3 --percent 100
```
Post-switch metrics: overall error rate dropped to 0.3%, p95 latency from 820ms -> 120ms. Queue depth at resv-east-2 decreasing.

claire-infra: Quota increase approved by cloud: +16 GPUs to project. Kicking autoscaler recovery.

bob-runtime: Autoscaler reconnected and started provisioning nodes into resv-east-2. New capacity detected +12 GPUs. Rebalancing in progress.

erin-cs: Notifying AcmeBank that we completed temporary move, autoscaler is restoring original pool, and we'll return them once rebalancing is done. Customer acknowledges, appreciates quick updates.

alice-oncall: Summary: root cause = cloud GPU quota exhaustion causing autoscaler failures; effect = reserved pool saturation and queue growth affecting AcmeBank; mitigation = emergency routing to standby pool + quota bump + autoscaler restart.

frank-platform: Postmortem notes: need automated fallback path for reserved tenants when autoscaler hits quota (runbook task). Also consider pre-warming standby pools for enterprise customers.

erin-cs: Follow-ups: I will sync with account team and schedule customer post-incident call.

alice-oncall: Closing incident for operational response. Creating follow-up tickets: infra-437 (quota monitor + alarm), runtime-512 (automatic reserved-failover), cs-118 (customer comms). Will update once postmortem is ready. :white_check_mark:
